items.title: Found, but Not Fixed : From Software Vulnerability Discovery to Fixes with Iterative LLM Pipelines
items.summary: The paper explores using iterative large language model pipelines to automate fixing software vulnerabilities after detection.
items.whyItMatters: It could speed up secure coding and reduce costly manual patching for developers.

items.title: Set-based State Estimation for Unknown Dynamical Systems from Noisy Output Data with Probabilistic Guarantees
items.summary: The paper presents a set-based state estimation method for unknown dynamical systems using noisy output data, deriving bounds on state set diameter and formulating a linear program for tightness.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a model-free, data-driven approach with probabilistic guarantees, useful for robust control and fault detection in uncertain systems.

items.title: An Interpretable Acoustic Coordinate System for Japanese Consonant Morae in Dysarthric Speech
items.summary: The paper proposes a visual feedback system using an interpretable acoustic coordinate framework for Japanese consonant morae to aid dysarthria rehabilitation.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers a novel, fine-grained, language-specific tool for speech therapy and AI-driven feedback.

items.title: Joint Learning of Factual and Counterfactual Worlds for Causal Prior-data Fitted Networks
items.summary: The paper discusses how to jointly learn factual and counterfactual outcomes for causal inference using synthetic data.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a new approach to estimate treatment effects when real data only shows factual outcomes.

items.title: Cache or Denoise Less? Residual Reuse in a Flow-Matching World Action Model
items.summary: The article compares caching versus reducing denoising steps in flow-matching robot policies using a 6B model on LIBERO-Goal.
items.whyItMatters: It informs efficient policy design for large-scale robotic planning.

items.title: Minimax Estimation of Discrete Distributions under Hockey-stick Divergence
items.summary: The paper studies minimax estimation of discrete distributions under hockey‑stick divergence, giving non‑asymptotic bounds and showing add‑constant estimators achieve them.
items.whyItMatters: It informs how many samples are needed for accurate distribution estimation in high‑dimensional settings.

items.title: Multiaccuracy as an Error Benchmark for Learning with Distribution Shift
items.summary: The paper proposes multiaccuracy as a benchmark for learning when training and test data come from different distributions.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a practical way to evaluate models under real-world distribution shifts.

items.title: Where Should LLM Agents Adapt at Test Time? In Context, in Weights, or Both
items.summary: The article explores how large language model agents can adapt during test time by storing experience in context and adjusting model weights, especially in repetitive environments.
items.whyItMatters: It shows ways to boost agent efficiency and personalization in real-world applications.

items.title: Data Attribution Should Steer Pretraining
items.summary: The article argues that pretraining should be guided by data attribution, using testable properties to select useful documents for model learning.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a smarter, cost‑effective way to improve AI performance by curating training data based on model knowledge.

items.title: MathaMAGICal: Validating Trajectory Data Attribution During Capability Acquisition
items.summary: The paper evaluates MAGIC, an influence-function method, on large GPT-2 models trained on arithmetic tasks to assess trajectory data attribution accuracy.
items.whyItMatters: It informs how well influence-based attribution predicts data removal effects in large language models.

items.title: Elicited Adaptation: Auditable Localized Fairness via Pairwise Queries
items.summary: The paper investigates how much a model’s scores must shift to maintain fairness when a community’s fairness standard changes, using pairwise similarity queries.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers a measurable, auditable method to adjust models for localized fairness.

items.title: RIFT: Reward Improvement Field Transfer for Cross-Domain Offline RL
items.summary: RIFT learns how source and target transitions differ in reward to improve cross-domain offline RL with limited target data.
items.whyItMatters: It enables better policy transfer when dynamics vary, boosting efficiency for tech‑savvy RL practitioners.

items.title: Attacker Diversity Reduction in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming
items.summary: Reinforcement learning can make automated red-teaming more successful while narrowing the attacks it produces. Co-training an attacker and a defender with group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) has been reported to reduce attacker diversity. This experiment reproduces attack diversity reduction using three runs with a Qwen2.5-14B attacker and a Phi-4-mini defender trained by direct preference…

items.summary: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical…

items.title: Architecting the Corporate AI Infrastructure: The Evolving Roles of AI Governance Committees and Chief Ethics Officers
items.summary: The accelerating integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into core business operations has created an urgent need for robust corporate governance infrastructures capable of managing complex ethical, legal, and operational risks. While organizations have increasingly adopted high-level AI ethics principles, a critical implementation gap persists: fewer than half of organizations that cite AI…

items.title: When AI Agents Should Repair, Replan, or Abandon: A Threshold Theory of Plan Commitment
items.summary: AI agents often discover mid-execution that their plan is broken, for example when an action fails or a tool is withdrawn. Deployed systems use conventions such as retry loops or "always replan," and a recent benchmark finds no fixed strategy dominates. This paper derives the optimal policy. items.title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
items.summary: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can capture the nanoscale physics of fracture at the atomistic level, but their computational cost prohibits predictions at the length scales and time scales needed for many applications. Machine learning approaches, on the other hand, have been proposed as heuristic surrogates for material fracture, yet they cannot guarantee the physical consistency of the…

items.title: BadGCL: Towards Persistent Backdoor Attack on Graph Continual Learning Systems
items.summary: Backdoor attacks pose a persistent security threat to machine learning systems, yet their behavior under graph continual learning (GCL) remains underexplored. Conventional graph backdoor attacks often lose effectiveness as models are updated across successive tasks, creating the impression that continual updates naturally weaken malicious associations. items.title: A Geometric Understanding of Denoising Autoencoder with Applications to Image Denoising
items.summary: Denoising autoencoders have shown strong empirical performance in recovering clean data from their noisy observations, yet their underlying statistical behavior remains underexplored. items.title: With the Right Representation, Classical Machine Learning Rivals Deep Models for Olfactory Mixture Similarity
items.summary: Modeling olfactory mixtures remains a critical challenge in machine olfaction because the task requires reasoning over relationships between sets of odorants rather than over individual molecules in isolation.
